title: Hardcoded pipe id u32(2) may target the wrong pipe in severance tests
evidence:
direct, _ := topology_apply_edit(&state.topology,
		Command{kind = Cmd_Draw_Pipe{a = router, b = h1, tier = std}}, cat, state.inventory, 1)
	...
	_ = direct
	return state
...
	// find the direct leg (router -> h1): the FIRST-drawn leg pipe
	direct := u32(2)
	occupied := on_pipe_count(&state.flow, direct)
detail: severance_fixture captures the real direct-leg id then discards it (`_ = direct`); the test hardcodes u32(2), contradicting its own comment. If pipe ids start at 0, u32(2) is router->j2, not router->h1.
recommended_fix: Return direct.pipe from severance_fixture and demolish that id, mirroring sibling test_severance_reroute_or_drop which uses `target = direct.pipe`.

title: Log roundtrip test validates only 2 of N command kinds
detail: The #partial switch checks only Cmd_Draw_Pipe and Cmd_Set_Pipe_Priority; Demolish/Upgrade/Place_Router/Set_Lane_Weights round-trip is silently unchecked, despite the byte-for-byte-semantics claim.
recommended_fix: Add a case (or default) asserting equality for every Command kind, so any unhandled or non-matching kind fails the roundtrip.

title: Dead variable sev_drops_before captured but never asserted
detail: sev_drops_before is read then referenced only in `_ = sev_drops_before`; no assertion uses it. Suggests an intended severance-drop check was dropped or forgotten.
recommended_fix: Either assert on sev_drops_before (e.g. drops increased post-demolish) or delete the capture and the `_ =` suppression.

title: Variable named `wide` binds the standard tier index
evidence:
wide, _ := tier_index(cat, "standard")
	cmds := []Command{
		{kind = Cmd_Draw_Pipe{a = host, b = router, tier = wide}},
		{kind = Cmd_Draw_Pipe{a = h1, b = h1, tier = wide}}, // self-loop
detail: `tier_index(cat, "standard")` is bound to a variable named `wide`, then used as `tier = wide`. The name contradicts the value, misleading future readers about the tier in use.
recommended_fix: Rename the binding to `std` / `standard_idx` to match the looked-up tier, or change the lookup to "wide" if wide was intended.
